questions.prompt: A running Azure VM can use the requested target size on its current host cluster. What should you still plan for when resizing it?

options.text: A VM restart and application interruption
options.explanation: Running-VM resizing is disruptive even without a separate deallocation requirement.

options.text: A guaranteed change with no guest restart
options.explanation: Availability of the SKU does not make resizing nondisruptive.
Resize changes resource allocation, not disaster recovery configuration.

options.text: Automatic expansion of every guest filesystem
options.explanation: Changing the VM size does not automatically extend all disk filesystems.

questions.prompt: A VM in an availability set needs a size unavailable on the current hardware cluster. Which operational consequence must be considered?

options.text: All VMs in that availability set may need to be deallocated.
options.explanation: This allows the set to be allocated on hardware that supports the new size.

options.text: Only changing its resource group guarantees the new size.
options.explanation: Resource-group membership does not select a different hardware cluster.

options.text: Increasing the OS disk guarantees the new size.
options.explanation: Disk capacity does not establish compute SKU availability.

options.text: Changing the display name forces a compatible cluster.
options.explanation: Resource naming does not control placement capacity.

questions.prompt: A resize operation fails, but the VM model now displays the requested larger size. What is the best next verification?

options.text: Check the operation failure, allocation state, and actual guest resources.
options.explanation: The model can show the requested configuration before successful allocation.

options.text: Conclude the larger size is active solely from the model field.
options.explanation: That field can reflect the failed requested change.

options.text: Assume the guest data disks were necessarily erased.
options.explanation: A failed compute resize does not establish data-disk deletion.

options.text: Delete the deployment history to complete the resize.
options.explanation: History deletion does not allocate new hardware.
